clinical_features.symptoms:
signs: Sinus tachycardia/new AF, hypertension, increased 
temperature 
* Causes: Graves’ disease, thyroid tumours, multinodular goitre, 
Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, TSH producing pituitary tumour, 
pregnancy related (Molar pregnancy), drug induced e.g. 
amiodarone, levothyroxine overtreatment 
* Differential diagnosis: Sepsis; heat stroke; anticholinergic / 
sympathomimetic drug intoxication; malignant 
hyperthermia; neuroleptic malignant syndrome; 
serotonergic syndrome; delirium tremens / 
withdrawal; pheochromocytoma; psychiatric / 
psychological conditions (diagnosis of exclusion) 
* Biochemistry: Usually high T3/T4, low TSH, except TSH producing pituitary 
conditions. Concomitant adrenal insufficiency – 
hyperkalaemia, hyponatraemia, hypoglycaemia 
* Risk stratification: Burch-Wartofsky scale to assess risk of Thyroid storm 
• ACUTE MANAGEMENT: 
Identify precipitant, screen and manage complications e.g. AF, consult 
endocrine to start antithyroid Rx/further workup 
• THERAPY: 
Carbimazole (Neo-mercazole) 20-60mg dly, titrate to effect. Propranolol 
40mg bd for symptom control. Definitive Rx Radioactive Iodine therapy 
 
 
 
HYPOTHYROIDISM 
*History: Fatigue/lethargy, cold intolerance, weight gain, cognitive 
impairment/slowed mentation, depression, coarse features, 
constipation. High index of suspicion in elderly, depressed pts 
*Examination: Dry skin, coarse hair, slowed speech/movement, pallor, 
hair loss, goitre, hoarseness, non-pitting oedema 
(myxoedema) 
* Vital signs: Bradycardia, hypotension, decreased temperature 
*Causes: Autoimmune thyroiditis, previous thyroid surgery/radioactive 
iodine treatment, dietary iodine deficiency, drug induced, 
pituitary pathology 
*Differential diagnosis: Sepsis; hypothermia, cardiac arrhythmias e.g. 
3rd degree heart block, slow AF; dementia; 
sedative intoxication; psychiatric/psychological 
conditions 
*Biochemistry: Usually low T3/T4, high TSH 
*Risk stratification: Screen for features of impending myxoedema coma 
*AC

warnings:
Caution in ADHF*: 
Propranolol 60-80 mg po 4hrly, OR 
Esmolol 250-500g/kg IV load over 1 min, then 50- 
100 g/kg/min IV 
• 
Methimazole 20-30mg PO 6hrly, OR 
Propylthiouracil 600-1000mg PO load, then 300mg 
PO 6hrly (max 1.2g/day) 
• 
Hydrocortisone 100mg IV stat then q8hrly OR 
Dexamethasone 2-4mg q6hrly 
• 
Lugol’s iodine 4-8 drops PO 6hrly – 60 minutes AFTER 
PTU/methimazole 
If Iodine allergy ➔ Li Carbonate 300mg 6 hrly 
• 
Consider antibiotics and sepsis workup 
• 
Plasmapheresis as last
